title: Red Dead Redemption 2
provenance: tested locally on Apple Silicon (M1 Pro), macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r5, 2026-09-10: loads to 98 per cent and never renders. Status stays community because there is no verdict for a title we tested and could not run.
notes: Does not run on this Mac as of 2026-09-10 (M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r5), and the reason is pinned down. The Rockstar Games Launcher signs in and hands off, RDR2 starts, opens a 1280x720 window that composites, loads to 98 per cent, creates its swapchain, and exits without presenting a frame. The game runs its own Vulkan renderer, and MoltenVK 1.4.1 refuses the images it asks for: 'vkCreateImage(): If tiling is VK_IMAGE_TILING_LINEAR, mipLevels must be 1' (3) and the same for 'imageType must be VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D' (16), the last three refusals immediately before the exit. Earlier in the run MoltenVK's shader translator emits Metal that will not compile (gl_CullDistance written into a vertex output struct that does not declare it) and Apple's driver logs about 10900 'AGX: Texture read/write assertion failed: bytes_per_row >= used_bytes_per_row' assertions. The signature is identical on every run (16/5/3/1/1/1). Highball's graphics mode applies only to the launcher, since this is the game's own Vulkan, not a Direct3D translation. Every route to the game's DirectX 12 renderer has been tried and is closed. There is no -dx12 switch: the exe knows -vulkan, -ignoreDifferentVideoCard, -safemode and -ignorepipelinecache, and nothing for DX12. The API is chosen only by Documents/Rockstar Games/Red Dead Redemption 2/Settings/system.xml, and a complete real file with <API>kSettingAPI_DX12</API> in its <advancedGraphics> block (schema taken from files the game itself wrote on Windows: root rage__fwuiSystemSettingsCollection, version 37, configSource kSettingsConfig_Safe), placed where the game demonstrably writes its own files, with -ignoreDifferentVideoCard in commandline.txt, still produced a Vulkan run with the file left untouched: the game never attempted D3D12 at all, because the D3D12 timestamp shim that was wired in for RDR2.exe alone (via HKCU\\Software\\Wine\\AppDefaults\\RDR2.exe\\DllOverrides) never loaded. Setting the graphics mode to D3DMetal instead breaks the launcher, which needs a Direct3D 10.1 device D3DMetal does not provide. Vulkan cannot be removed to force the issue because RDR2.exe hard-imports ffx_fsr2_api_vk_x64.dll, which hard-imports vulkan-1.dll (status c0000135). Disabling amd_ags_x64 changed nothing. Two leads remain, both engine work: RDR2.exe queries two DXGI interfaces Wine's DXGI does not know (f0db4c7f-fe5a-42a2-bd62-f2a6cf6fc83e and a4966eed-76db-44da-84c1-ee9a7afb20a8, unidentified, possibly a capability probe that decides the API), and MoltenVK would need to accept or emulate linear-tiled images with mip levels. The fix belongs in the engine, not in settings. Note for anyone retrying: about eight launcher starts in one evening ended with the Rockstar launcher failing to sign in on every fresh start, so test in one session.

knownIssues.symptom: Loads to about 98 per cent, opens a window, then exits without showing a frame.
knownIssues.cause: the game's own Vulkan renderer asks MoltenVK for linear-tiled images with more than one mip level, which MoltenVK 1.4.1 refuses. Its DirectX 12 renderer cannot be selected: there is no command line switch for it and the settings file that chooses the API is not honoured on this setup.
knownIssues.fix: none today. This needs a change in MoltenVK or in the engine's DXGI, not a setting.
